'''Kawasu Matsuri''' (川裾祭) is a festival held at river confluences and near river mouths. It is also known as '''Kawasu-san''' or '''Kawasso-san'''. Additionally, "Kawasu" can be written as '''川すそ''' or '''川下'''.
== Overview ==
Kawasu Matsuri is observed in various regions from {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|en|Fukui Prefecture|qid=Q133879|lt=Fukui Prefecture|1=Fukui Prefecture}} to the northern part of {{ill|Hyōgo Prefecture|en|Hyōgo Prefecture|qid=Q130290|lt=Hyōgo Prefecture|1=Hyōgo Prefecture}}, with some festivals having religious significance. Generally, these festivals take place at river confluences or near river mouths, but some are also held along coastlines distant from river mouths.
== Major Kawasu Festivals ==
; {{ill|Takashima, Shiga|en|Takashima, Shiga|qid=Q845794|lt=Takashima, Shiga|1=Takashima, Shiga}}, {{ill|Makino, Shiga|en|Makino, Shiga|qid=Q6739696|lt=Makino, Shiga|1=Makino, Shiga}}
: The Kawasu Matsuri here is the annual festival of {{ill|Karasaki Shrine (Takashima)|ja|唐﨑神社 (高島市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Karasaki Shrine (Takashima)|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, located near {{ill|Lake Biwa|en|Lake Biwa|qid=Q200239|lt=Lake Biwa|1=Lake Biwa}}. It is held on the fourth Sunday of July and is the only major summer festival in the Kosai region.
; {{ill|Takashima, Shiga|en|Takashima, Shiga|qid=Q845794|lt=Takashima, Shiga|1=Takashima, Shiga}}, {{ill|Shin'asahi, Shiga|en|Shin'asahi, Shiga|qid=Q7497069|lt=Shin'asu, Shiga|1=Shin'asahi, Shiga}}
: The Kawasu Matsuri (also known as "Yamagata no Kawasu-san") is the summer festival of the subsidiary {{ill|Karasaki Shrine (Takashima)|ja|唐﨑神社 (高島市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Karasaki Shrine (Takashima)|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} of {{ill|Nishinomiya Ōjinja|ja|西宮大神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishinomiya Ōjinja|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} near Lake Biwa. Once held on July 28, it is now observed on the last Sunday of July, featuring traditional dances for entertainment until late at night.
; {{ill|Ichijima, Hyōgo|en|Ichijima, Hyōgo|qid=Q5986143|lt=Ichijima, Tanba|1=Ichijima, Hyōgo}}, [[:en:Tanba, Hyōgo|Tanba, Hyōgo]]
: The {{ill|Ichijima Kawasu Matsuri|ja|市島川裾まつり|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichijima Kawasu Matsuri|1=Ichijima Kawasuso Matsuri|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q113636826}} is a river festival held along the {{ill|Takeda River (Hyōgo and Kyoto)|ja|竹田川 (兵庫県・京都府)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeda River (Hyōgo and Kyoto)|1=Takeda River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11599330}}, a tributary of the {{ill|Yura River (Japan)|en|Yura River (Japan)|qid=Q11577617|lt=Yura River (Japan)|1=Yura River (Japan)}}. Taking place on July 29, it features floating lanterns and a fireworks display of around 750 shells. Other related festivals in Tanba City include the "Ganso Kawasu Matsuri" in {{ill|Hikami, Hyōgo|en|Hikami, Hyōgo|qid=Q5760340|lt=Hikami, Hyōgo|1=Hikami, Hyōgo}}, "Kita Goi Kawasu Matsuri," and "Naramatsu Kawasu Matsuri."
; {{ill|Shin'onsen, Hyōgo|en|Shin'onsen, Hyōgo|qid=Q1154955|lt=Shin'onsen, Hyōgo|1=Shin'onsen, Hyōgo}}, {{ill|Mikata District, Hyōgo|en|Mikata District, Hyōgo|qid=Q1155035|lt=Mikata District, Hyōgo|1=Mikata District, Hyōgo}}
: The Kawashimo Grand Festival is a river festival held at the {{ill|Kishida River|ja|岸田川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kishida River|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Kuto River|ja|久斗川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuto River|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and {{ill|Tai River|ja|田井川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tai River|1=taigawa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q16282088}}. As the annual festival of {{ill|Utono Shrine|ja|宇都野神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utono Shrine|1=Utsuno- Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q109594469}}, it includes performances of the {{ill|Kirin Shishi-mai|ja|麒麟獅子舞|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kirin Shishi-mai|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 麒麟獅子|1=Qilin dance|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11677329}}, designated as an Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property of Hyōgo Prefecture. The festival features a procession of mikoshi (portable shrines) and a large fireworks display with around 3,000 shells, recognized as one of the {{ill|Three Great Festivals of Tajima|ja|但馬三大祭り|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Three Great Festivals of Tajima|1=Tajima Three Great Festivals|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11381623}}.
; {{ill|Amino, Kyōtango|ja|網野町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amino, Kyōtango|1=Amino|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11607240}}, {{ill|Kyōtango|en|Kyōtango|qid=Q513897|lt=Kyōtango, Kyoto|1=Kyōtango}}
: The {{ill|Asamogawa Minazuki Matsuri|ja|浅茂川水無月祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Asamogawa Minazuki Matsuri|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (commonly known as "Kawasso-san") is held annually on July 30 in Asamogawa, Amino, Kyōtango. The festival includes a sea-going mikoshi procession and concludes with a large summer fireworks display.
